hooks.text: A tiny star is screaming out of our galaxy forever.
Can a star escape the Milky Way galaxy forever?
This star is moving way too fast for our galaxy.

title: A Star ESCAPING the Milky Way
description: Citizen scientists discovered a rare object moving so fast it's leaving our galaxy forever.

beats.text: A tiny star is screaming out of our galaxy forever.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a star being ejected from the Milky Way's disk, 2024

beats.text: It is moving at about one million miles per hour.
beats.visual: Animation showing a star moving rapidly across a background of distant stationary stars

beats.text: Citizen scientists found this rogue object using NASA infrared data.
beats.visual: NASA Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE) spacecraft in orbit, artist's concept

beats.text: Volunteers spotted it while hunting for a hidden ninth planet.
beats.visual: A person at a computer monitor reviewing infrared astronomical data from the Zooniverse project

beats.text: This object is a rare, low-mass star called an L subdwarf.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a cool, dark red L-type subdwarf star in deep space

beats.text: The speeder is only four hundred light-years away from Earth.
beats.visual: Map of the local Milky Way neighborhood showing the Sun and the position of CWISE J1249+3621

beats.text: One theory says an exploding white dwarf kicked it away.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of a Type Ia supernova explosion in a binary star system

beats.text: Or binary black holes catapulted it like a cosmic slingshot.
beats.visual: Animation showing a black hole binary slingshotting a small star into space

beats.text: This ancient relic is now on a one-way trip and it's never coming back.
beats.visual: View of a lone star receding into the dark void of intergalactic space

better_than_last: Integrated emotional high-stakes payoff in the final beat and an animated black hole slingshot visual as requested by the reviewer.
